message.content: {"4": {"original": "discrimination against music lovers", "rephrased": "Students characterize the University of Oxford's ban on the peer-to-peer music service Spotify as discrimination against music lovers, arguing that restricting access to a legal service based on usage type is unfair. This stance highlights a conflict between the university's bandwidth management goals and the students' expectation of equal access to digital resources for both academic and recreational purposes.", "summary": "Students view the university's ban on Spotify as discriminatory against music lovers."}, "5": {"original": "see nothing wrong with students using Spotify", "rephrased": "Some students at the University of Oxford maintain that there is nothing wrong with using the legal peer-to-peer music service Spotify, rejecting the notion that the service's data-sharing model inherently justifies a blanket ban. This perspective challenges the university's argument that the service consumes excessive network bandwidth, suggesting that usage levels are not universally problematic.", "summary": "Some students argue that using the legal music service Spotify is not inherently wrong."}, "6": {"original": "The university provides free internet access for students because it's aneducat", "rephrased": "The University of Oxford justifies its provision of free internet access to students as an essential educational resource, asserting that recreational use is permissible unless it consumes enough bandwidth to degrade network performance for others. This position frames the restriction on the peer-to-peer service Spotify as a necessary technical measure to preserve academic functionality rather than an arbitrary limitation on student freedom.", "summary": "The university justifies internet restrictions on Spotify as necessary to preserve bandwidth for academic purposes."}, "7": {"original": "Bandwidth that seems insignificant for one user will soon add up when scaled up", "rephrased": "The University of Oxford's Computer Services department explains that while the data usage of a single student using the peer-to-peer service Spotify appears negligible, the cumulative effect across thousands of connected users creates a significant strain on the university's network infrastructure. This technical reality underpins the department's decision to block the service, prioritizing the stability of the network for high-demand academic activities over individual recreational listening.", "summary": "The university's IT department argues that individual Spotify usage is insignificant but becomes a major network burden at scale."}}
